subject: Electrical Engineering
title: The Bipolar Transistor: Current Controls Current
description: A 60-second lesson on The Bipolar Transistor: Current Controls Current.

hook.text: A tiny current into the base unleashes a much larger current from collector to emitter.

buildup.text: The BJT has three layers: NPN or PNP. The thin base region is the key.

discovery.text: Base current lowers the barrier. Collector current flows — amplified by a factor called beta.

twist.text: No base current means no collector current. The transistor is a switch and an amplifier.

climax.text: Early transistor radios replaced bulky vacuum tubes and launched portable electronics.

punchline.text: A whisper at the base becomes a shout at the collector — that's amplification.

quiz.question: How does a bipolar transistor amplify signals?
options: It generates energy from heat to boost the signal
A small base current controls a much larger collector current
It stores charge and releases it in bursts
